correctness.rationale: A product of distinct reflections moves exactly their two-dimensional span: rank is at most two, rank zero would give equal factors, and a rank-one isometry is a reflection and has determinant -1. For an anisotropic second normal in W_g, shortening g inverse and reversing the resulting pair gives a unique factorization of g. Spinor multiplicativity imposes ab=theta(g). The three binary-form cases give (q-eta)/2 lines per class, q lines of the unique nonzero class, or no anisotropic lines. Identity fibers count same-class reflections, and the standard fixed-norm quadratic-form counts give the two ambient formulas. In dimension three every nonidentity oriented element has rank two (eigenvalue 1 by reciprocal eigenvalues and determinant 1; rank one is excluded), and every moved plane has an anisotropic line. For each such plane, Wall matrices have symmetric part the Gram matrix S and alternating part parametrized by t. Determinants det(S)+t^2 give respectively q-2,q,q-1 admissible parameters for split, nonsplit, and rank-one restrictions. The quadratic character sum -1 for nonzero det(S) yields the spinor-sign counts; the rank-one parameter has square determinant and the hyperbolic plane splitting shows its sole nonzero norm class is kappa. Orthogonal complements of normal lines give exactly q(q+1)/2, q(q-1)/2 and q+1 planes of the respective types, hence the four spectrum rows. The uniform benchmark q^3/(q^2-1) is strictly between q and q+1, so only identity and nonsplit targets enter the positive deviation sum, yielding the exact TV expression. For nondegenerate planes there are two allowed ordered pairs with ab=theta(g), each having the stated fiber size.
residual_risks: The deposited checker does not run over extension fields; the Wall correspondence and finite-field character calculation apply over all odd prime powers. No nonzero fibers at moved rank two with totally singular restriction are inferred from missing observed products; they follow from the anisotropic-normal requirement.

evidence: SO_3(q) identifies with PGL_2(q), with a reflection mapped by central negation to a projective involution; its kappa-type is the split involution class. Split involutions lift to the fixed GL_2 involution class. A projective ordered pair has four sign lifts and the two opposite lifts of the target have equally many factorizations, so the GL_2 fiber divided by two gives the projective fiber.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This proves actual same-channel equivalence after normalization, not merely a resemblance between parameters. The split-class product is spinor-positive; it is not the walk that samples both projective involution classes.
